clue.text: One qualified to guide holy group

parts.note: PI is the standard short form of pious, holy
a lot is a group or batch of things

explanation.surface: A person fit to lead a religious community.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a licensed navigator who steers ships or aircraft safely.

clue.text: It takes time, proverbially

parts.note: the proverb calls putting things off the thief of time, so this habit takes time in the sense of stealing it

explanation.definitionFit: Habitual delay is proverbially the thief of time, so it literally takes time away.

clue.text: Left port with cargo

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship that sailed out of harbour fully loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A laden vessel is loaded or burdened with goods.

clue.text: Switch off and go on strike

definitions.meaning: to extinguish a light, as in putting the lamp out
workers are said to come out or walk out in a stoppage

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to extinguish a lamp and, in older usage, for workers to strike.

clue.text: Cheeks city men

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England
chaps is an informal word for men

explanation.surface: Impudent behaviour from urban gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH CHAPS are cured pig's cheeks, a West Country delicacy; the surface pushes 'cheeks' towards cheekiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath chaps are the salted lower jaw and cheek meat of a pig.

clue.text: Intimate blessing

explanation.definitionFit: A boon companion is a close friend, and a boon is a godsend or benefit.

clue.text: Encourage midshipman to be receptive and relax

parts.note: to take it is to accept or put up with what comes
Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of Captain Marryat's 1836 naval novel

explanation.surface: Telling a young naval officer to be open-minded and calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Encourage' frames the charade as a call to the midshipman: 'Take it, Easy!'
explanation.definitionFit: To take things calmly is to rest and avoid strain.

clue.text: Muslim leaders clash violently about religious uprising

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the other piece
violently implies being thrown about, so the letters are scrambled
in a down answer an uprising means the word is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: PI is short for pious, religious

explanation.surface: Islamic rulers fight fiercely over a revolt of the faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violently' rearranges CLASH, which goes 'about' IP, from PI turned by 'uprising'.
explanation.definitionFit: Caliphs were the civil and religious successors of Muhammad as heads of the Islamic community.

clue.text: Taking into custody for striking

explanation.definitionFit: The word means detaining by police and also attention-grabbing or impressive.

clue.text: Very brief tenure of office for Christian, for example

definitions.meaning: read literally, being in charge for just a moment
Fletcher Christian was the deputy officer of HMS Bounty who led the mutiny

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally it is control lasting a moment; Fletcher Christian was the deputy to Captain Bligh.

clue.text: Prepare to read more into record of work pending

definitions.meaning: to get something more to read, you would place an order for a volume
a firm's ledger of orders received but not yet fulfilled

explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the phrase is an instruction to request a volume; as a business term it is the list of unfilled orders.

clue.text: Expressing writer's emotions in the theatre

definitions.meaning: ... poetry voices the poet's personal feelings
a well-known theatre on Shaftesbury Avenue in London's West End

explanation.definitionFit: Lyric verse is personal, emotional poetry, and the Lyric is a famous London playhouse.

clue.text: Chance for Smollett's hero

definitions.meaning: used adjectivally, as in a chance meeting: haphazard, unplanned
Roderick ... is the title hero of Tobias Smollett's 1748 novel

explanation.definitionFit: Something haphazard happens by chance, and Roderick is the surname-bearing protagonist of Smollett's picaresque novel.

clue.text: Model daughter in a soap given full scope

indicators.note: to model is to shape or fashion, so the following letters are remoulded into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl who sits for artists is cast in a TV serial and given free rein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun describing the daughter, but it is the anagram signal working on D + IN + A + SOAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A diapason is the entire compass or range of a voice or instrument, hence complete scope.

clue.text: Ignorant as some policemen are about one point

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: police on the beat wear uniform, unlike detectives in plain clothes
N, north, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Constables who are unaware of a certain matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ignorant is to lack knowledge or information about something.

clue.text: Material possessions that may be abused

definitions.meaning: matter or stuff of which something is made
wealth, as in a man of means and property
drugs or alcohol, the object of the phrase ... abuse

explanation.definitionFit: The word means physical matter, wealth (a person of means), and a drug, as in the phrase about its abuse.

clue.text: Fish round stern of boat, standing up

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the fish's letters go about the letter from the boat

parts.note: a brisling is a small sprat-like fish, often canned

indicators.note: the stern is the back end of a boat, so the word's final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A fish circles the back of a vessel, upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair or fur that is bristling stands erect, as on an angry animal.

clue.text: Some terrific stories around in this genre

indicators.note: the run taken from the words is turned round to read the other way
only some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run lying within them

explanation.surface: A few great tales belong to this type of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes IFICS from 'terrific stories'; 'around' turns it to give the answer. 'Stories' in the surface fits the genre neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction is a literary and film genre of futuristic and technological stories.

clue.text: Man following one daughter's peculiar expression

indicators.note: the island's letters are placed after the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
D is the abbreviation for daughter
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A fellow trailing after somebody's girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea, abbreviated IOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a phrase peculiar to a language whose meaning is not literal.

clue.text: Anaesthetic producing extra apprehension when taken orally

indicators.note: taken orally means spoken, so the words are a sound-alike of the answer

parts.note: extra means more, and apprehension means fear

explanation.surface: A painkiller that causes extra anxiety when swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken orally' suggests swallowing a drug but signals a soundalike, in a non-rhotic British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Morphia is an old name for morphine, an opiate painkiller and sedative.

clue.text: Agnostic Liberal sadly yearning for the past

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unbeliever of the Liberal party is wistful about the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' looks like part of the sentiment but signals an anagram of AGNOSTIC plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a wistful longing for times gone by.

clue.text: Took on commercial work Edward contracted

parts.note: an ad is a commercial or advertisement
OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the pet name is cut down at its end

parts.note: Teddy is a familiar pet form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A man named Edward took on some advertising work for a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt is to take on or assume, as a child, a policy or a name.

clue.text: Waiter's here with no meat or rum

indicators.note: rum here is the adjective meaning odd or strange, signalling the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A restaurant server is present with neither food nor spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the adjective 'strange', the anagram signal; 'Waiter's here' means where someone waits, not a server.
explanation.definitionFit: An anteroom is a small waiting area leading to a larger room, where one waits to be admitted.

clue.text: Weaver's seat

definitions.meaning: Nick ... is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream; the 's stands for is
the part of the body one sits on

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comic weaver bears this name, and it also means the buttocks one sits on.

clue.text: Sailor needing books and cards

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A seaman who needs reading and a deck of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot is a deck of picture cards used in fortune-telling.

clue.text: Bishop served with fish in accommodating vicar's home

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A bishop is served fish at the parsonage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vicar of Bray, in an old song, changed his faith with each monarch to keep his living: an accommodating vicar, and Bray is in Berkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berkshire village is the parish of the turncoat cleric in the traditional song.

clue.text: Girl getting husband in a temper

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman who is angry with her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The noun meaning temper is dated slang, as in getting someone's Irish up.
explanation.definitionFit: In old slang, to have one's Irish up is to be roused to anger, so the word means a temper.

clue.text: Retrograde plan involving the Speaker in temporary suspensions

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece surrounds the other
retrograde means moving backwards, so the word for plan is read in reverse

parts.note: an aim is a plan or intention
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: A backward-looking scheme involving the Commons chairman leads to temporary halts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Speaker' suggests the presiding officer of the House of Commons, but here it is any public speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A moratorium is a legally authorised pause or delay; the Latin plural is used here.

clue.text: What's annoying, about tough Cockney being tight-fisted

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: niggly means irritating or nagging
hard, said by a Cockney who drops the h, becomes 'ard

explanation.surface: An irritating hard man from London's East End is stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner whose accent drops the initial h, so HARD becomes ARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggardly person is mean and stingy with money.

clue.text: Old-fashioned Democrat on Fourth of July, say

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means coming after, so the party letter follows

parts.note: the Fourth of July is an example of a calendar date

explanation.surface: A traditional American politician at Independence Day celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dated is out of style, belonging to an earlier time.
